objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026), on John's idea that loops of logic are like eddies in a river shared across the universe, 'core-libs' kind of processing: (1) settle which cycles of knots give self-feeding exponential growth (eddies) and why the many cycles of large growers do not, by a rule read from the candidate map, frozen-tested on the census's rings and on the cycles of SCALE-SHARE's growers, every ring confirmed by real growth (the cluster rule can report false rings: CLUSTER-ALL's second break); (2) build a catalogue up to a stated size of distinct self-feeding loops (patterns, not descriptions), each with its ratio as a root of its equation, whether it is the same under not-all-equal, and its interface (what joining a chain, a spare or another loop does to its ratio); (3) say whether the catalogue is finite, a few families or unbounded, and whether a small generating set composes the rest. Serves G17.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Partially successful, 8 of 14 held as scored, 3 more post hoc; referee pending; part U pending): an eddy is a loop of open knots with two ways round, rare because large starts' knots are full; the rate solves W = 1 for the loop's round-weight; inside the cluster rule's domain the minimal eddies to eight knots are one family (x^(L+1) = x + 1), identical under not-all-equal, with interfaces that multiply W; the rule's break shapes hide more eddies.
stop_rule: One pilot (fitting), one frozen run, read-out, referee hand-off, report.
title: Which loops of knots feed themselves? A catalogue
